newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian PM confirms that wants to resign.
newsitem.headline: Estonian PM confirms that wants to resign.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi said on Wednesday that he intended to resign his post as soon as political parties have decided on the formation of a new government.

Vaehi said in a statement that he was confirming his decision to resign and was clearing up confusion after saying on Tuesday he would lead talks to try and enlarge his current minority administration. He said some newspapers had mistakenly intepreted this as meaning he wanted to remain premier.
"Under the present balance of political powers, there is no point for me to continue as prime minister," Vaehi said.

"I have decided to step down as prime minister as soon as political parties have agreed on forming a new government enjoying parliamentary support and have also found a candidate for prime minister," he added.

Vaehi's position became untenable after he only narrowly won a parliamentary no-confidence vote on Monday. The vote gained the support of 45 MPs in the 101-seat parliament while 46 deputies backed the premier.
Vaehi currently leads a minority administration with the definite backing of 41 MPs and five or six independent deputies.
